newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zurich loses banking jobs for first time.
newsitem.headline: Zurich loses banking jobs for first time.

text.p: The number of jobs provided by Swiss banks in the city of Zurich, the financial capital of Switzerland, fell for the first time between 1991 and 1995, the city's statistics office said.
The number of people employed in banks and financial institutions fell by 8.8 percent to 36,311 in 1995 from 39,809 in 1991, the office said, based on a survey from September 1995.
But comparing 1995 employment levels with 1985, the number of jobs rose by 14.1 percent, the office added.
Overall, the number of jobs in Zurich fell 11.2 percent, or by 40,103, to 317,188 between 1991 and 1995. Compared with 1985 the number of jobs in Zurich fell 5.3 percent.

Jobs provided by the services sector in Zurich fell 8.7 percent to 265,545 between 1991 and 1995, while jobs in the secondary sector, such as industry, construction and crafts, fell 22.3 percent to 51,643.
In the canton, or region of Zurich, there was an 8.3 percent fall in the overall number of jobs between 1991 and 1995 to 691,747. From 1985 to 1995 there was a 4.5 percent increase.

For the whole of Switzerland, there was a 5.9 percent decline in the number of jobs between 1991 and 1995 to 3.54 million. Comparing 1995 with 1985, the was an 8.0 percent rise in the number of jobs, the office said.
